text:
IncidentBot: :rotating_light: P1 Alert - Dedicated pool dp-helios-prod reaching GPU exhaustion for tenant_helios. Pager triggered.
Maya: acknowledged, I'm oncall. Whats the pool status?
Tom: dp-helios-prod (12 gpus) flipped to 100% at 2026-03-15T18:14:28Z. Tenant `helios-main` occupying all GPUs. Sudden surge in streaming+batch combo.
Devin (CS): Helios ops just messaged our support channel: spike in inference latency and timeouts, their dashboard shows queued inference jobs piling. They say they did not deploy any job changes.
Priya: do they have burst enabled or a contractual auto-scale?
Devin (CS): contract shows "burst=false". No auto-burst. They are VPC + dedicated; we cannot spill to shared pools without approval.
Lucas: quick snapshot from ops-tools:```\n$ rwdctl pool show dp-helios-prod --short\npool: dp-helios-prod\ngpus: 12/12 in use\ntenants:\n  helios-main: 12 gpus, 93 active sessions\npending_queue: 412 requests\navg_95_latency: 3.8s\nautoscale: disabled\nburst_policy: none\n```
Maya: ugh. Two immediate paths: (A) emergency temporary burst (if cloud capacity available), (B) session-level mitigation (evict/terminate or throttle heavy sessions), (C) model shedding to smaller quantized variant, or (D) ask customer to kill problematic jobs.
Tom: cloud account has limited preemptible capacity in region; infra may be able to allocate up to +6 GPUs in ~10-15m, but we only have limited preemptible quota. If not, we could attempt to reassign some idle GPUs from warm pools but that would impact capacity elsewhere.
Priya: check whether we can do a model downgrade fallback. We have a smaller quantized variant `gpt-small-q4` that is compatible with their features; quality will drop but latency improves and requires ~0.4 GPUs per instance vs 0.9 for main model. Could reduce pressure if we migrate a portion of sessions.
Devin (CS): customer explicitly said "do not drop active sessions" unless unavoidable. They'll accept billed burst or degraded model as long as sessions persist.
Maya: agree. Proposed plan: 1) Attempt emergency burst of up to 6 preemptible GPUs; 2) In parallel, create a proportionate model-shedding route for new requests (10-20%) to `gpt-small-q4` to relieve token serving; 3) If queue > 300 after 20m, start controlled eviction of longest-idle sessions (graceful 30s drain) with customer consent.
Tom: commands to run (requires infra approve and account exec signoff):```\n# request burst GPUs\nrwdctl pools burst-allocate dp-helios-prod --count 6 --ttl 45m --reason "P1 tenant saturation"\n# create weighted routing rule\nrwdctl routes create --pool dp-helios-prod --route "route_id=helios-shed,match=tenant=helios-main,weight=0.15,target_model=gpt-small-q4"\n# start session eviction (controlled)\nrwdctl sessions evict --pool dp-helios-prod --tenant helios-main --strategy oldest-first --grace 30s --max=10\n```
Priya: I'll message infra lead for burst approval. Maya, can you authorize eviction policy if we reach the threshold?
Maya: I will authorize eviction only after 20m and only with CS approval.
Devin (CS): pinged account exec in Helios channel. They replied: "approve billed burst up to $8k immediate; no session kills without ops coordination." Sending confirmation.
IncidentBot: Provisioning update - allocation requested, status: pending (ticket 9034).
Tom: infra says preemptibles are scarce; they can only guarantee 2 GPUs right now. We need fallback if full 6 unavailable.
Maya: proceed with 2 GPUs then; start model shedding rule to 30% (higher relief) while we try to get more capacity.
Priya: applying routing rule now.```\n$ rwdctl routes create --pool dp-helios-prod --route "route_id=helios-shed,match=tenant=helios-main,weight=0.30,target_model=gpt-small-q4"\nRoute helios-shed created and activated.\n```
Tom: burst allocate returned: 2 GPUs allocated (ETA 8m). Pool status now:```\n$ rwdctl pool show dp-helios-prod --short\npool: dp-helios-prod\ngpus: 14 total (12 base + 2 burst), 14 in-use\ntenants:\n  helios-main: 14 gpus, 110 active sessions\npending_queue: 260\navg_95_latency: 2.6s\n```
Devin (CS): customer reports improvement in tail latency within 6 minutes. They still see intermittent spikes but better than before.
Maya: good. Next: gather telemetry to understand surge origin. Was there a traffic surge, client-side retry loop, or a runaway job?
Priya: pulling session creation rates and model-run durations for helios-main between 17:50-18:20 UTC. Also checking whether they auto-run batch backfills.
Tom: note: model shedding may cause some higher CPU usage on orchestrator for conversions; monitor control plane.
IncidentBot: new updates will be posted to ticket 9034.
A few minutes later...
Priya: early findings: a misconfigured retry loop in helios SDK caused clients to open long-lived streaming sessions when they didn't receive prompt acknowledgements. Spike in session creation rate from ~5s avg to 150ms bursts around 18:05. KV cache grew 3x due to retained receivers.
Maya: that explains it. Plan for immediate postmortem: root cause is client retry config + lack of tenant-level per-session caps.
Devin (CS): CS will coordinate with Helios to fix their SDK (backoff) and to apply a server-side safety net. They've agreed to a change window tonight.
Tom: SRE follow-ups: - implement tenant-level GPU soft cap (e.g., 10/12) with explicit override on contract, - add automatic model-shed route if pending_queue > 200 for >5m, - add session TTL eviction for long-idle receivers.
Maya: capturing assignments: Priya -> RCA and traces; Tom -> implement queue-triggered model-shedding prototype; Lucas -> session-eviction tooling and runbook; Devin (CS) -> customer coordination and approval notes.
Priya: I'll prepare preliminary RCA and timeline; aiming for EOD.
Maya: handoff: I'm stepping off in 25m. Priya, you're primary for RCA and follow-ups, Lucas will be backup oncall.
Priya: taking over oncall and investigation. I'll post updates here.
IncidentBot: Incident P1 assigned to Priya for investigation. Time open: 00:36.
Maya: thanks everyone. Quick comms: tell Helios we provisioned 2 emergency GPUs, applied model shedding to 30% for new requests, and identified a client retry bug. We're coordinating an SDK patch with them tonight.
Devin (CS): message sent to customer; they responded: "appreciate the fast help, please share RCA and next steps." :thumbsup:
Maya: closing the active paging loop; keep thread for RCA and postmortem artifacts. If any regression, @channel. Great work. :clap:
